sentences.text: Today, we are going to talk about something we all use every day.
WhatsApp is one of the most popular messaging apps in the world.
We use it to chat with friends, send messages, make calls, and share pictures or videos.
But what if you need to use WhatsApp in English?
Sometimes we have to message an English -speaking friend, colleague, or customer.
Maybe you are learning English and want to practice chatting.
That's why today's episode is all about how to communicate in English on WhatsApp.
How to use emojis and abbreviations.
Seven, common WhatsApp problems and solutions.
By the end of this episode, you will feel more confident using WhatsApp in English.
When you message someone on WhatsApp, you usually start with a greeting.
If it's a friend, you can be casual.
If it's someone you don't know well, you should be polite.
Polite greetings for work or new people.
I have a quick question about the meeting tomorrow.
WhatsApp messages are usually short and simple.
People don't write long sentences in a chat.
Can you send me the document?
Did you see my last message?
Can you help me with my homework?
Could you send me the address, please?
Would you mind sending me the report?
I need help with my English homework.
On WhatsApp, people use emojis and abbreviations to make messages faster and more fun.
By the way, I don't know.
Don't use too many abbreviations in formal conversations.
If you don't want to type, you can send a voice message.
Before sending a voice message, you can say, Hey, I'll send you a voice message.
Can you listen to my message?
I just wanted to check if we are still meeting at 3pm.
Try to speak clearly in voice messages so the other person can understand you easily.
You can also call someone on WhatsApp if you don't want to text.
Before calling, you can message, Hey, can I call you now?
Are you free for a quick call?
During a call, you can say, Can you hear me?
I think the connection is bad.
If the person does not answer, leave a message.
Hey, just checking if you saw my message.
No rush, but let me know when you have time.
I think my internet is slow.
Now you know how to speak English on WhatsApp.
One, use short and clear sentences and messages.
Two, use polite language when chatting.
Three, don't use too many abbreviations and formal messages.
Four, always check your messages before sending.
Speak clearly in voice messages and calls.
I hope this episode helps you feel more confident using WhatsApp in English.
If you liked this episode, please subscribe to my podcast.
